article_content: John Lewis CEO Andy Street has apologized for describing France as a place where 'nothing works and nobody cares.' Yet recent economic data suggests his harsh assessment may hold truth. In September, France recorded its fifth consecutive month of economic contraction, as businesses continued to lay off workers at the fastest rate in 16 months. Analysts now warn that France is no longer just the 'sick man of Europe' — it's becoming the 'sick man of the world.' Though France’s overall economy is 1.2% larger than its pre-crisis peak in early 2008, this growth is almost entirely driven by public spending. When government expenditure is excluded, private sector output remains 1.7% below 2008 levels — a clear sign the private economy is technically back in recession. Chris Williamson, Chief Economist at Markit, noted that the 'increasingly bloated' public sector has masked deep weaknesses in business investment and productivity. Unemployment hovers above 10%, with over three million people out of work. Private consumption — traditionally the engine of French growth — is under severe pressure. Firms remain hesitant to invest due to falling profits and mounting uncertainty about the future. Adding to the crisis is political turmoil. President François Hollande is the most unpopular leader in French history, his reputation shattered by personal scandals — including an affair with actress Julie Gayet and a bitter public split from his partner Valérie Trierweiler. His administration’s perceived ineffectiveness has accelerated the rise of Marine Le Pen’s far-right National Front, which recently won its first two seats in the French Senate after dominating local elections.

article_content: After spending 14 years in prison for a crime he didn’t commit, 29-year-old Lorenzo Montoya was set free following the overturning of his murder conviction. New DNA tests proved he wasn’t involved in the 2000 killing of Emily Johnson, a 29-year-old special education teacher in Denver. Although Montoya had confessed under pressure during police questioning as a 14-year-old — a statement later ruled inadmissible — he always denied involvement in the murder itself. The real killer, 16-year-old Nicholas Martinez, stole Johnson’s car and beat her to death. The next day, Montoya and friends took a joyride in the vehicle, believing it had been legally purchased. Montoya was convicted based on circumstantial evidence like a sneaker print and a jacket, neither of which contained his DNA. In 2011, attorney Lisa Polansky took his case pro bono and fought for years to get it reopened. After the Colorado Bureau of Investigation confirmed the DNA mismatch, prosecutors offered Montoya a deal: plead guilty to being an accessory to murder in exchange for immediate release. Having already served more than the 10-year sentence tied to the accessory charge, he walked out of court a free man. Montoya, who spent four of those years in solitary confinement, showed remarkable grace, telling his lawyer he harbored no bitterness. He plans to leave Denver behind, earn his GED, and learn a skilled trade. His attorney described him as one of the most kind-hearted people she’s ever known — still learning how to use the internet, but full of hope for what comes next.

Kuna ta oli juba teeninud rohkem kui 10-aastane trahv, mis oli seotud osalemisega, läks ta kohtust vaba meheks. Montoya, kes veetis nende aastatest nelja üksinduses, näitas imelikku armastust ja ütles oma advokaadile, et tal pole viha. Ta plaanib jätta Denveri taga ja omandada GED ja oskustöö. article_content: By Marie-Louise Olson. PUBLISHED: 15:14 EST, 11 September 2013. | UPDATED: 15:58 EST, 11 September 2013. Romantic stories of men gallantly placing their coats over puddles to protect their partners’ feet from getting wet aren’t just medieval fairy tales. Today’s teenagers in love will go to great lengths to show how much they care. When this young Mexican couple—nicknamed 'Romeo and Julieta' by their friends—found themselves caught in a heavy downpour, the boyfriend decided to prove his devotion. He picked up his girlfriend and carried her through deep floodwaters, determined to get her to safety. But before he reached dry ground, an unseen hole beneath the water’s surface swallowed them whole. Fortunately, their laughing friends had captured the entire moment on camera. Who says chivalry is dead? Carrying her safely: 'Romeo' lifts 'Julieta' to carry her across the flooded street. Danger ahead: He believes he’s heading to safety—but then... Whoops!: A hidden hole opens beneath them. Going, going... gone!: The pair vanish under the water. In shock: They resurface, drenched and startled. Soaking wet: Romeo emerges holding his dripping backpack. Helping hand: He reaches for Julieta’s hand to pull her out. Quick check: They quickly assess whether either was injured. Follow me: Julieta takes the lead, grabbing Romeo’s hand. I could’ve sworn...: A bewildered Romeo glances back at the spot where the hole vanished.

article_content: James E. Holmes, a 24-year-old former neuroscience doctoral student, is being remembered by those who knew him as reserved, studious, and dependable — traits that seem almost impossible to square with the violence police say he unleashed at a packed Aurora movie theater. In the days following his arrest, a fragmented picture has emerged: a brilliant student who excelled academically, yet vanished from public view just weeks before the attack. Holmes graduated with top honors from UC Riverside in 2010 before enrolling in a doctoral program at the University of Colorado’s Anschutz Medical Campus. Faculty recall him as intellectually sharp, even expected to present research on microRNA biomarkers in May 2012. Yet in June of that year, he abruptly withdrew — offering no explanation. Authorities confirm he had no prior criminal record, aside from a minor traffic citation in 2011. What stands out now is the scale of his preparations. Over the past four months, Holmes received dozens of packages to his home and lab — materials police believe helped him arm himself with four guns and more than 6,000 rounds of ammo. On the night of the shooting, witnesses described a figure in full tactical gear — helmet, vest, gas mask — moving silently through the theater. His face? Never seen. There’s no trace of Holmes on Facebook, Twitter, or Instagram. But investigators are examining a now-deleted profile on Adult Friend Finder, featuring a man with fiery red hair, identifying as a 24-year-old from Aurora. Some officers suspect it’s him — possibly an alter ego tied to the 'Joker' persona he reportedly claimed upon arrest. Those who lived near him describe a solitary tenant who kept odd hours — loud techno music often blasted from his apartment, timed to start automatically after he left. One neighbor nearly walked in, unaware the place was rigged with explosives. Bomb squads later disabled the traps, allowing residents to return home. His past includes volunteer work at a summer camp for underprivileged kids — a stark contrast to the chaos he allegedly caused. Friends and family in San Diego, where he grew up, struggle to reconcile the polite, clean-cut young man they knew with the suspect in headlines. The Holmes family released a brief statement expressing grief for victims, declining to comment further. As investigations continue, officials stress the attack was carefully planned. What remains unclear is why — and how someone so seemingly ordinary became capable of such horror.

Holmes, 24-aastane endine neuroteaduse doktorant, on meelde jäetud nende poolt, kes teda tundsid, kui tagasihoidliku, õppivana ja vastutustundlikuna — omadused, mis tunduvad peaaegu võimatuks kokkupandavad vägivaldsega, mida politsei ütleb, et ta avaldas täis teatris Auroras. Tema vahistamise järgsetel päevadel on ilmunud hajakas pilt: geniaalne õpilane, kes oli akadeemiliselt esikohal, kuid kadus avalikust vaatest hetke enne rünnakut. Holmes lõpetas UC Riverside’i 2010. aastal kõrgeima hindega enne kui ta astus sisse Colorado Ülikooli Anschutzi meditsiinikampusse doktorantide programmisse. Õppejõud mäletavad teda intellektuaalselt tugevana, isegi ootasid, et ta esitaks uuringu mikroRNA biomarkerite kohta mai 2012. Kuid juunis sel aastal ta loobus programmist — ei andnud põhjust. Politsei kinnitab, et tal ei olnud eelnevaid kuritegulisi kirjeid, välja arvatud väike liiklusvõrrand 2011. aastal. Mida nüüd silma paistab, on tema valmistumise ulatus. Viimaste nelja kuu jooksul sai Holmes suure arvu pakette oma kodu ja labori aadressile — materjale, mida politsei usub, et ta kasutas, et varustada end neli relvaga ja üle 6000 lauaga. Rünnaku ööl kirjeldasid silmevaatajad figuuri täielikus taktilises varustuses — kaelakapp, rindkapp, gaasimask — liikudes vaikseselt teatri sees. Tema nägu? Mitte kunagi nähtud. Holmesel pole jälg Facebookil, Twitteril ega Instagramil. Kuid uurijad uurivad nüüd kustutatud profiili lehel Adult Friend Finder, kus on mees põleva punase juuksedega, kes identifitseeris end 24-aastasena Aurorast. Mõned politseinikud usuvad, et see on ta — võib-olla alter ego, mis on seotud 'Jokeri' personaadiga, mille ta kinnitas vahistamisel. Nendega, kes temaga lähedal elasid, kirjeldati üksinda elavat tenanti, kes hoidis paarilise ajakava — kuuldavalt helistas teatris muusika, mis käivitus automaatselt pärast tema lahkumist. Üks naaber tõusis peaaegu sisse, ei teades, et ruum oli püstitatud plahvatusmängudega. Bombitehnikud deaktiveerisid hiljem ohud ja lubasid evakueeritud elanikud tagasi minna. Tema minevik hõlmab volikäikude tööd lastekampsusel vajavate laste jaoks — vastandus kõige kõrgemale kohale, mida ta süüdistatakse. Sõbrad ja perekond San Diegos, kus ta kasvas üles, kannatavad, et kõrvutada kõnekaunis, puhas noormees, keda nad tunsid, süüdlasega. Holmesi perekond avaldas lühese avalduse, väljendades kurbust ohvritele, keeldudes lisateavest. Uuringud jätkuvad, kuid ametnikud rõhutavad, et rünnak oli hästi planeeritud. Mida veel ei ole selge, on miks — ja kuidas keegi nii tavapärane sai võimeliseks sellise hirmutava häbiväärsuseks.

article_content: Crystal Palace have been told to match Blackburn Rovers’ £5 million valuation of Rudy Gestede or abandon their pursuit in the January transfer window. The Premier League club is offering £3.5 million for the striker, but Blackburn have warned that their refusal to accept Hull City’s £10 million bid for his strike partner Jordan Rhodes last summer demonstrates they will not be pressured into a discounted sale. Manager Gary Bowyer said: 'I think the owners have set a valuation, and until it’s met, I don’t believe he’ll be leaving. They proved that this season with Jordan Rhodes.' Blackburn Rovers striker Rudy Gestede sat out his side’s 1-1 draw with Wigan Athletic at the DW Stadium. The forward is attempting to secure a move to Premier League side Crystal Palace. 'The conversation has been straightforward: any offers received by the club are passed to the owners, who make the final decision. We are under no instruction to sell, but we must present every offer to them. Obviously, no deal has been done yet — so both parties are negotiating over the right price.' Although Gestede was initially reported to have missed last weekend’s game due to being out of sorts, Bowyer insisted the 26-year-old Benin international was rested because Blackburn believed a transfer was imminent. He also confirmed Gestede will feature in Blackburn’s upcoming FA Cup tie against Swansea City on Saturday: 'There’s been no question about the player’s mindset at all. If you saw him this morning throwing himself around in training, you’d know he’s in a great place. He’s a good person who just gets on with his job.' Gestede has scored 24 goals in 43 league appearances for Blackburn. 'We thought the deal might progress faster than it has — that’s why he wasn’t selected against Wigan. With no further developments, he’s in the squad for Saturday. Unless something changes, he’ll focus on preparing for Swansea.' 'He’s conducted himself brilliantly. It’s not his fault the valuation hasn’t been met. All he can do is prepare for the game.' Bowyer gave a wry response to comments from Gestede’s agent, David Wancier, who claimed the player 'really wants to sign for Crystal Palace but is also committed to Blackburn.' 'It would be interesting if another Premier League club came in,' Bowyer said. 'There’s nobody at the moment, but that might make his agent think. I can only speak on Rudy’s behalf — and he’s been fine. He’s committed to playing on Saturday. His relationship with our fans is fantastic, and I’m sure they’ll be chanting his name. There’s no doubt he’ll give 100% — that’s the kind of lad he is.' Gestede celebrated scoring the equalizer for Blackburn against Middlesbrough in November.

article_content: The World Health Organization (WHO) has requested detailed information from China regarding a sharp increase in respiratory illnesses among children, including pneumonia, as top pediatric hospitals across the country face overwhelming patient loads. The WHO referenced reports—such as one from ProMED, a global infectious disease tracker—that highlighted an outbreak of 'undiagnosed pneumonia in children in northern China.' In a statement released Wednesday, the international health body urged Chinese officials to provide additional epidemiological, clinical, and laboratory data. This surge coincides with China’s first winter since lifting its strict COVID-19 pandemic controls, and children appear to be disproportionately affected. Local media report a steady rise in mycoplasma pneumoniae infections among kindergarten and primary school students. While this bacterium typically causes mild cold-like symptoms in older children and adults, it can lead to prolonged pneumonia in younger children, with symptoms lasting weeks. Data from the Chinese CDC shows influenza positivity rates climbing steadily in October, even as COVID-19 cases remain low following a brief summer peak. At Beijing Chaoyang Hospital—the nation’s leading respiratory disease center—mycoplasma positivity among children reached 40%, compared to just 6% in adults, according to Vice Dean Tong Zhaohui, who spoke at a recent briefing. Mycoplasma outbreaks typically occur every three to seven years, and experts warn that treatment is becoming increasingly difficult. Up to 80% of pediatric cases and 60–70% of adult cases show resistance to azithromycin and related antibiotics, said Dr. Yin Yudong of Chaoyang Hospital. This has triggered a surge in demand at top children’s hospitals, where emergency wait times now exceed seven hours in some cases. To alleviate pressure on major hospitals, China’s National Health Commission (NHC) is enhancing local clinic capacity to detect and treat infections early, according to Xinhua. Despite China’s tiered healthcare system—designed to funnel patients through community clinics—many families bypass lower-level providers and head directly to elite urban hospitals, as referrals are not mandatory. Public awareness is growing: masks are increasingly visible on Beijing’s subways, and teachers are urging parents to keep symptomatic children home. Meanwhile, Beijing and Tianjin CDC branches report that mycoplasma infections have peaked, though influenza and RSV cases are continuing to rise, as reported by CCTV and other state media.
translated_content: Maailma Terviseorganisatsioon (MTO) on palunud Hiinalt detailset infot kõrgeima tasemega lastearstide haiglates toimuvast tugevast hingamisteede haiguste tõusu, sealhulgas soomusest, kuna kõikide riigi esiletõusnud lastekliinikud on patsientidega ülekoormatud. MTO viitab raportitele, sh ühele viimasel nädalal ProMEDilt, mis jälgib nakkushaiguste levikut maailmas ja mille kohaselt on Põhja-Hiinas esinenud 'diagnoosimata soomust lastes'. Kolmapäeval avaldatud avalduses palus rahvusvaheline tervishoiuasutus hiinlastel esitada täiendavat epidemioloogilist, kliinilist ja laboratooriumi andmeid. See tõus langeb kokku Hiina esimese talvega pärast nende rangete COVID-19 pandeemia piiranguid lahtivõtmist, ja lapsed näivad olevat eriti mõjutatud. Kohalikud ajalehed raporteerivad püsivast kasvust mykoplasma pneumoniae nakatumises lasteaia ja põhikooli laste seas. Kuigi see bakter põhjustab tavaliselt ainult kergeid külmetuslike sümptomeid vanematel lastel ja täiskasvanutel, võib see nooremate laste puhul põhjustada pikendunud soomust, mille sümptomid kestavad nädalaid. Hiina Tervishoiu Kontrolli- ja Ennetuskeskuse andmete kohaselt tõusis influentsi positiivsusmäär oktoobris järjepidevalt, kuigi COVID-19 juhtude arv jääb madalaks pärast suve lühikest tippu. Pekingi Chaoyangi haigla, riigi juhtiv hingamisteede haiguste keskus, teatas, et mykoplasma positiivsus laste seas on tõusnud 40%-ni, kuid ainult 6%-ni täiskasvanute seas, kui haigla asejuhataja Tong Zhaohui rääkis viimase nädala ajal pressikonverentsil. Mycoplasma epidemiat toimub tavaliselt iga kolme kuni seitsme aasta tagant, ja ekspertid hoiatavad, et ravi muutub üha raskemaks. Kuni 80% laste ja 60–70% täiskasvanute juhtude puhul ei reageeri ravimile azüthromütsiinile ja sellele klassile kuuluvatele antibiootikumidele, ütles Chaoyangi haigla nakkushaiguste arst Dr. Yin Yudong hiljuti Pekingi uudistes. See on põhjustanud suure hulga pereid otsima abi esmaklassiliste lastehaiglate juures, kus kiire abi osakonna ootamisaeg on mõnel juhul ületanud seitse tundi. Suuremate haiglate koormuse vähendamiseks suurendab Hiina Rahvuslik Tervishoiukomisjon (NHC) kohalike kliinikute võimet tuvastada ja raviada nakkusi varasel staadiumil, kui Xinhua teatas neljapäeval, viidates mitteidentifitseeritud NHC ametnikule. Kuigi Hiinal on olemas tasehaldussüsteem, kus kohalikud kliinikud teenindavad elanikke esmase tervishoiu kujul, otsivad paljud perekonnad otse suurte linnade prestiižsemaid haiglaid, kuna viidet ei ole vaja. Avalik teadlikkus kasvab: maskid on üha rohkem nähtavad Pekingi tihedatel metroolindadel, ja õpetajad paluvad vanematele hoida lapse kodu, kui ta näitab sümptomeid. Samas teatasid Pekingi ja Tianjini CDC filiaalid, et mykoplasma infektsioonid on saavutanud tipu, kuid influentsi ja hingamisteede süntsiitsiaalviiruse (RSV) juhtudel on tõus jätkunud, kui teatasid CCTV ja teised riiklikud meediakanalid.

article_content: A new study warns that the recommended 21-day quarantine period for the Ebola virus may not be sufficient to prevent transmission. While the World Health Organization (WHO) states the incubation period ranges from two to 21 days — meaning individuals without symptoms after three weeks are unlikely to be infected — researchers at Drexel University in Philadelphia have found a 12% probability that the virus can remain dormant beyond this window. This finding suggests a significant portion of the population in West Africa could develop symptoms outside the established incubation period, undermining current containment strategies. Professor Charles Hass, a biologist with extensive experience in pathogen risk analysis, noted that previous estimates relied on limited data from outbreaks in Zaire and Uganda, which showed minimal variation in incubation times. However, data from the 1995 Congo outbreak and recent West African cases indicate greater variability. In a paper published in PLOS Currents, Hass argues that while the 21-day standard was reasonably derived from early data, it may no longer be adequate for public health protection. He emphasizes the need for a systematic evaluation of the trade-offs between the costs of extended quarantines and the risks of premature release. Hass stressed that for highly transmissible and lethal pathogens like Ebola, the consequences of under-quarantining are severe. His goal is not to prescribe a new duration, but to propose a method for determining optimal quarantine periods based on risk-benefit analysis.
translated_content: Uus uuring hoiatab, et soovitatav 21-päevane karantiiniperiood Ebolaviiruse jaoks võib olla piisavalt lühike, et takistada levikut. Kuigi Maailma Terviseorganisatsioon (MTÜ) seob inkubaatiaajaks vahemiku kahe kuni 21 päeva — tähendades, et isikud, kes ei arenda sümptomeid kolme nädala jooksul, ei ole tõenäoliselt nakatunud — on Drexeli Ülikooli Philadelphia osakonna teadlased leidnud, et viirusele on 12% tõenäosus jääda vaiksesse olekusse selle perioodi ületavale ajale. See leiutis viitab sellele, et Lääne-Aafrika populatsiooni oluline osa võib arendada sümptomeid eelneva inkubaatiaaja välistatud ajal, mis rikub praegused kontrollstrateegiad. Bioloog ja patogeenide riskianalüüsija professor Charles Hass märkis, et eelmised hinnangud pohinesid piiratud andmetel Zairi ja Uganda väljade puhul, kus inkubaatiaaja variatsioon oli minimaalne. Kuid andmed 1995. aasta Kongo väljast ja viimastest Lääne-Aafrika juhtudest viitavad suuremale variatsioonile. PLOS Currents'i avaldatud artiklis väidab Hass, et kuigi 21-päevane standard oli loogiliselt põhjendatud varaste väljakutsete andmetega, võib see enam ei ole piisav avaliku tervise kaitseks. Ta rõhutab vajadust süsteemselt hinnata pikendatud karantiinide kulusid ja ennetamata vabastamise ohtu. Hass rõhutas, et kõrge levivuse ja surmavusega patogeenide puhul, nagu Ebola, on alama karantiini järgimise tagajärjed väga tõsised. Tema eesmärk ei ole määrata uut perioodi, vaid pakkuda meetodit optimaalse karantiini kestuse määramiseks riski ja kasu analüüsi alusel.

article_content: Court documents reveal that Jeffrey Epstein, the convicted financier and child abuser, maintained an extensive network of contacts among global elites — including former U.S. President Bill Clinton, British royals, and international celebrities. The records, submitted as evidence in a civil lawsuit filed by women alleging abuse by Epstein, include 97 pages of phone numbers, email addresses, and home addresses. Among them: 21 contact entries for Bill Clinton and his staff, all listed under the name of Epstein’s former advisor, Doug Band. Epstein’s so-called 'Holy Grail' — a digital contact log — reportedly contained coded entries for dozens of women labeled 'massage,' believed by investigators to refer to underage victims. One former employee, Alfredo Rodriguez, stole the file and tried to sell it to attorneys seeking evidence, leading to his conviction for obstruction of justice. Prince Andrew, the Queen’s second son, is named in the documents with 16 distinct contact details, including numbers for Balmoral and Sandringham — royal residences where Epstein was a guest. These details emerge amid renewed allegations that he engaged in sexual activity with Virginia Roberts, then a 17-year-old minor, orchestrated through Epstein’s network. Other prominent names include former UK Prime Minister Tony Blair and Lord Peter Mandelson (with ten entries); former Israeli Prime Minister Ehud Olmert (three numbers); and celebrities such as Mick Jagger, Ivana and Ivanka Trump, Liz Hurley, Barbara Walters, and Richard Branson. Epstein also recorded contact information for luxury venues like The Plaza in New York, Claridge’s in London, and the Beverly Hills Hotel. His connection to Sarah Ferguson, Prince Andrew’s ex-wife, is underscored by an agreement in December 2010 to pay £15,000 to settle her debts — a transaction occurring shortly after his release from prison for soliciting prostitution from minors. The documents do not imply that listed individuals were involved in illegal activity. However, the sheer volume of high-profile contacts raises serious questions about the extent of Epstein’s influence and the boundaries of elite social circles. Rodriguez, who called the journal his 'insurance' fearing Epstein would silence him, served 18 months in prison. Epstein, meanwhile, denied the journal contained any relevant information — even claiming names like Donald Trump had 'no connection whatsoever' to his crimes.

article_content: David Cameron has pledged to reduce net migration to 'tens of thousands'. A Daily Mail survey found that 80% of voters oppose granting free access to UK jobs for Romanian and Bulgarian citizens starting January 1, 2014. Ministers warn that blocking such access could trigger legal action from the European Union, potentially resulting in fines from the European Court of Justice. Yet, nearly two-thirds of respondents said they would support defying EU rules—even if it meant legal penalties—to preserve national control over immigration. Eighty percent of voters believe Westminster, not Brussels, should decide who enters the UK. An overwhelming 85% said migration is placing excessive pressure on schools, hospitals, and housing. According to the MigrationWatch think tank, up to 70,000 migrants from Romania and Bulgaria could arrive annually, threatening Cameron’s target. Only 11% of respondents trust the Conservative Party on immigration—six points below Labour and 11 below UKIP. A striking 44% expressed no trust in any political party on immigration. Cameron has highlighted that net migration has fallen by a third since 2010 to 176,000, but 80% of the public still consider this level too high. Two-thirds of respondents agreed with former Labour Home Secretary Jack Straw that opening borders to Eastern Europeans in 2004 was a 'spectacular mistake'. Seventy-nine percent felt they were not adequately consulted about those 2004 policies, which contributed approximately 2.5 million to the UK population. Just 19% believed mass immigration has benefited British society overall; 64% disagreed. Forty percent said immigration had negatively affected their communities, versus 11% who said it improved them. Seventy-six percent believe it has made it harder for young Britons to find jobs. Older voters are especially concerned: over 90% of those aged 55+ support maintaining restrictions, compared to 72% of 16–24-year-olds. Romania and Bulgaria joined the EU in 2007 but were subject to transitional controls limiting work access until January 1, 2014. Immigration Minister Mark Harper stated the UK cannot legally extend these controls beyond the deadline without amending EU accession treaties—an action requiring unanimous consent from all member states, including Romania and Bulgaria. A surge in applications from Romanian and Bulgarian students for taxpayer-funded tuition grants—5,000 applicants, or one in six of all vocational course applicants in England—has raised concerns about fraud, prompting a temporary pause on all EU student aid applications. A No. 10 spokesperson defended the government’s record, claiming it has reduced net migration, shut down fraudulent colleges, and capped non-EU worker visas.

article_content: Published: 13:59 EST, 19 September 2013 | Updated: 17:49 EST, 19 September 2013 An illegal immigrant who married the now-Archbishop of York claimed £138,000 in public benefits and made a £60,000 profit by selling her council house back to a cash-strapped local authority. Rebecca Muwonge, 47, entered the UK from Uganda in 1996 using the identity of her 18-year-old niece, Proscovia Kasozi, and immediately applied for short-term housing benefit. The London Borough of Newham granted her temporary accommodation twice under this false name, while she used her real identity to claim benefits from the London Borough of Enfield. In 1996, Muwonge married Samuel Bisaso at Holy Trinity Church in Tulse Hill, south London. The ceremony was conducted by John Sentamu, who later became Archbishop of York in 2005. Sentamu later ordained Bisaso as a clergyman in the Church of Uganda, and Bisaso went on to serve as a chaplain for the Mission to Seafarers charity in Immingham, near Grimsby. The couple’s marriage deteriorated, and though they never divorced, Muwonge entered into a second marriage while separated from Bisaso. Muwonge, now residing in Keelby, Grimsby, pleaded guilty at Snaresbrook Crown Court to two charges: false accounting and obtaining property by deception through failure to disclose changes in circumstances. Bisaso and Muwonge were both convicted of immigration offenses in 2011 and sentenced to 18 months in prison. Muwonge gave birth to one of her five children while incarcerated. To secure rehousing, Muwonge submitted a forged letter claiming homelessness, allegedly written by her brother-in-law. After being rehoused by Newham, she applied for another council property in Enfield. She purchased her Newham property under the Right-to-Buy scheme at a steep discount. Later, the council repurchased it from her, resulting in a profit of over £60,000. Muwonge was arrested following a joint investigation by the two boroughs. Bisaso denied three counts of conspiracy to commit fraud at the latest hearing. Prosecutors acknowledged their case against him rested solely on his marital status to Muwonge and cohabitation. Muwonge continues to apply for British citizenship. She will be sentenced on 27 September 2013.

article_content: On Saturday, Asiana Airlines Flight 214, a Boeing 777, crashed during its approach to San Francisco International Airport. Flight data revealed the plane was traveling far slower than the required 137 knots — just 106 knots at the moment of impact. Despite the stall warning sounding seconds before collision, the pilots only attempted to abort the landing 1.5 seconds prior — too late to prevent disaster. The pilot flying the plane, though seasoned with over 10,000 total flight hours, had only 43 hours of experience in the 777 model and was making his first landing at SFO in this aircraft type. Meanwhile, the Instrument Landing System for Runway 28L had been offline for weeks, requiring the crew to rely on visual cues under clear skies — a scenario that may have increased workload and reduced margin for error. The aircraft struck the seawall just before the runway, causing the tail to detach. Both engines remained active at impact: one was found jammed against the fuselage, the other lying far ahead in the grass. Fire erupted mostly after the plane came to rest on its belly. Two 16-year-old Chinese students, Ye Mengyuan and Wang Linjia, died in the crash. One may have been fatally struck by an emergency vehicle — a tragic possibility still under investigation. Passengers reported chaos inside: overhead bins fell, and a life raft inflated within the cabin, trapping a flight attendant until others pulled her free. Air traffic control recordings show no emergency call was issued before impact. The NTSB is reviewing cockpit voice recordings and plans to interview the four crew members. Investigators are also examining whether the lack of automated guidance systems, combined with unfamiliarity with the aircraft, contributed to the crew’s failure to recognize their dangerously low altitude.

article_content: The Ebola High-Level Protection Suit — available on Amazon for just $1,300. The internet was flooded with products claiming to protect against the deadly Ebola virus, which had so far claimed one death in the U.S. An infectious disease expert today dismissed the panic-buying of 'Ebola protection kits' as a waste of money, noting that the only practical use most members of the public would have for a hazmat suit is as a Halloween costume. Protective suits, face masks, and survival kits were flying off shelves amid rising panic following the death of Thomas Eric Duncan on Wednesday and the hospitalization of two others. A total of 48 people are being monitored for possible symptoms. Online retailers are offering isolation gowns, surgical masks, booties, and even duct tape, falsely claiming to provide full protection against the virus. Preparation kits often include surgical masks, gloves, biohazard bags, and sanitizer wipes. Prices vary: a basic kit costs around $50 per person, while a high-level 'Level A' suit is listed on Amazon for $1,300. The bright blue suit, more suited to a space mission than a grocery run, is labeled a 'Level A Suit' and features a back-entry PVC face shield, attached gloves, and three layers of fabric with proprietary barrier films, spunbond nonwoven substrate, and inner barrier films. However, Dr. Amesh Adalja, an infectious disease specialist at the University of Pittsburgh and member of the Infectious Diseases Society of America’s public health committee, told MailOnline: 'These suits are a waste of money. Ebola does not pose a risk to the general public because it is not contagious unless you come into direct contact with the bodily fluids of a symptomatic individual.' He emphasized that the virus does not spread through casual contact like the common cold and urged Americans to prioritize flu vaccination — a far greater annual threat. Dr. Alexis Thomas, a physician practicing in London, echoed this sentiment: 'Panic buying of personal protective equipment — such as hazmat suits — is unnecessary and inappropriate. Ebola transmits only through direct contact with blood or body fluids of an infected person. Unless you're providing direct care to someone with confirmed Ebola symptoms and recent travel from an endemic region, wearing or purchasing such gear is pointless and fuels misinformation.' Companies like Med-Tech Resource and Mountainside Medical Equipment are marketing kits for $20–$25, claiming CDC approval. Yet, neither company can guarantee protection against Ebola. Med-Tech Resource’s website describes its kit as 'the ultimate protection and prevention kit for Ebola, influenza, and other outbreaks,' but declined to comment on sales volume. Meanwhile, nearly 40 self-published 'Ebola survival' e-books have appeared on Amazon in the past month. Titles include 'Ebola: Natural Remedies + Government Conspiracies' and 'Ebola Survival Guide 2015: 10 Things You Must Know to Survive the Coming Ebola Outbreak!' — the latter warning that 'Ebola could infect 4.1 billion people over the next 24 months.' Dr. Adalja advised the public to rely on WHO and CDC websites for verified information. Thomas Eric Duncan, a 42-year-old Liberian national, became the first U.S. Ebola fatality after arriving in the U.S. on September 20 and being hospitalized on September 28 — after being initially sent home with antibiotics. Ten of the 48 contacts are considered high-risk. Meanwhile, Sgt. Michael Monnig, a Dallas sheriff’s deputy not among the monitored group, sought care with Ebola-like symptoms; his test results were pending. Five U.S. citizens have been diagnosed with Ebola: Thomas Eric Duncan (deceased), Kent Brantly, Rick Sacra, Nancy Writebol, and Ashoka Mukpo. Three have recovered; Mukpo was quarantined in Nebraska, and a WHO doctor is being treated in Atlanta. More than 3,500 people have died in West Africa since the outbreak began in Guinea in December 2013. The public reaction echoes the SARS outbreak over a decade ago, which infected 8,000 and killed nearly 800 worldwide.

article_content: Former U.S. Army private Kevin Scott Sutay has been released by Colombia’s Revolutionary Armed Forces (FARC) after being held captive for four months. He was freed in a quiet handover in the southeastern region of Guaviare — the same area where he vanished in June 2013 while traveling as a tourist. Sutay, 28, was formally transferred to Norwegian and Colombian authorities, accompanied by the International Committee of the Red Cross. He was later received by U.S. officials at Bogotá’s airport at 11:30 a.m. local time. A Red Cross doctor confirmed he was fit to travel and reunite with his family. The FARC had captured Sutay on June 20, suspecting him of being a U.S. intelligence agent due to items found in his possession — including a GPS device and a military-style uniform. However, local residents and journalists who encountered him in the jungle described him as a confused, non-Spanish-speaking tourist simply trying to reach the Venezuelan border. His release was intended by FARC as a goodwill gesture to support ongoing peace talks — negotiations that began 11 months ago aimed at ending a 50-year civil conflict. But Colombian President Juan Manuel Santos refused to allow a public spectacle, rejecting FARC’s request to involve Reverend Jesse Jackson in a ceremonial release. No photographs or live footage were made public. U.S. Secretary of State John Kerry publicly thanked Colombia’s government for its 'tireless efforts' and acknowledged Jackson’s advocacy. Sutay was the only known foreign national held by FARC. His military service record shows he served as a combat engineer from 2009 to 2013, including a one-year deployment in Afghanistan ending in 2011. His hometown is Willow Spring, North Carolina. Attempts by The Associated Press to contact Sutay’s family following his capture were unsuccessful.

article_content: (CNN) — The fall TV season can be a hit or miss affair — and networks and viewers alike often decide quickly. Fox Show' and 'Sean Saves the World' (NBC): Both feature beloved actors but have underperformed. Variety included them on its list of the '10 Coldest TV Shows of the Fall.' • 'Hostages' (CBS): Low ratings make a second season unlikely. • 'Betrayal' (ABC): Despite its premise centered on infidelity, ratings have declined, and critics question its longevity, per TV Guide. • 'Back in the Game' (ABC): Starring James Caan, this sitcom has failed to connect with audiences. article_content: Arsène Wenger has firmly dismissed rumors that Joel Campbell will leave Arsenal this summer, making it clear the 22-year-old forward is central to his plans for the new campaign. Although Campbell’s standout performances for Costa Rica at the 2014 World Cup sparked speculation about a potential Premier League loan move, Wenger insists the player will be available for selection in the upcoming Emirates Cup matches against Benfica and Monaco. Campbell, who signed for Arsenal in 2011, has spent much of his time since on loan at Lorient, Real Betis, and Olympiacos — gaining valuable experience across three European leagues, including the Champions League. Despite interest from clubs like AC Milan and Galatasaray, both Campbell and Wenger are aligned on his future: staying in North London. Wenger also praised the growing influence of South American players at the club, highlighting new signings David Ospina and Alexis Sánchez. He noted that in certain positions — especially up front — South American talent often outshines its European counterparts. 'If you rank the world’s best strikers today,' he said, 'they’re overwhelmingly from South America.' Campbell himself told The Sun he considers the Premier League the most exciting in the world and views playing for Arsenal as his lifelong dream. With over 100 professional appearances under his belt and two goals in Brazil, he’s confident he can thrive at the highest level — and now has the opportunity.

article_content: A gang of twelve youths ransacked 45 mobile phone shops across London during a three-month spree last summer, stealing handsets and tablets worth hundreds of thousands of pounds. According to evidence presented at Croydon Crown Court, the group stormed stores—often pushing innocent bystanders aside, crowding customers, and violently wrenching devices from displays, sometimes still connected to wiring. The gang, aged between 17 and 19, primarily targeted Carphone Warehouse, O2, and Vodafone outlets. They operated in groups of four to twelve, coordinating meetups at transport hubs before launching coordinated attacks between June and August 2012. Following an intelligence-led operation by the National Mobile Phone Crime Unit (NMPCU), all members were arrested and later pleaded guilty to one count of conspiracy to commit burglary. Sentencing took place in February 2013. Christopher Street, 19, from South Norwood, received an eight-month jail sentence, suspended for 12 months, along with 200 hours of community service. Simon Hibbert, 18, of Thornton Heath, was handed a 12-month sentence, suspended for two years, plus 200 hours of community service. Laphaniel Fisher, 18, of Streatham, was jailed for nine months. Nyron Worrell, 18, of Thornton Heath, received a 12-month sentence suspended for two years. Kwasi Owusu Amankwaa, 18, also of Thornton Heath, is due to be sentenced next month. Seven members of the gang, aged 17, cannot be named due to legal restrictions. Two youths from Croydon were jailed for 12 months each; two others from Croydon received sentences of 18 and nine months. A 17-year-old from Lambeth was jailed for 12 months, and another 17-year-old from Croydon received an 18-month youth rehabilitation order. A third 17-year-old from Croydon failed to appear in court, and a warrant has been issued for his arrest. Detective Chief Inspector Robert Mahoney of the NMPCU said: 'Thanks to the hard work and dedication of NMPCU officers, a 12-member Croydon-based street gang has been successfully convicted of serious offenses committed across London. These convictions send a clear warning: the Metropolitan Police will robustly and swiftly tackle those who use intimidation to satisfy their greed.'

article_content: Pascale Sherwin, a 23-year-old nanny, was convicted of stealing dozens of personal items from the family she cared for in Exeter, Devon. The thefts—ranging from designer clothing and jewelry to sunglasses and luggage—began in early 2012, shortly after she started working full-time for Becki and Bradley Cannings. Sherwin, known to the family as 'Sasha,' had become a trusted figure, helping with everything from daily childcare to attending significant family events like the couple’s wedding and their daughter Olivia’s naming ceremony. The discovery came when Becki’s mother noticed Sherwin wearing stolen items in photos posted on Facebook—even tagged in some. Horrified, Becki printed the images and reported them to police, but authorities requested stronger evidence. In response, the Cannings installed four indoor and one outdoor camera. Within minutes of reviewing the footage, they captured Sherwin stealing a cardigan and stashing it in her bag—and the pattern continued across three consecutive days. When police searched Sherwin’s home, they found a cache of stolen belongings. At Exeter Crown Court, Sherwin admitted to the thefts. Judge Erik Salomonsen emphasized the severity of the crime due to the profound breach of trust. She was sentenced to 200 hours of unpaid community service. Becki Cannings described the experience as emotionally shattering. 'I felt violated,' she said. 'I never once suspected her—she was family.' Despite the evidence, she initially clung to hope it was a misunderstanding. Bradley, who owns an electrical engineering firm, expressed fury that Sherwin showed no remorse. 'She hasn’t even apologized,' he said. 'It makes my blood boil.' Though the family has moved forward—Olivia, now nearly three, will soon start preschool—Becki says she will never again entrust her child to anyone outside close family. 'I just wish I hadn’t let my guard down,' she added. 'I was so sure it wasn’t her.'

'Ma tahan lihtsalt, et ma poleks oma hoiaku langetanud,' ta lisas. 'Ma olin nii kindel, et see ei olnud ta.'

article_content: Tens of thousands gathered in Yaroslavl for a solemn memorial honoring the victims of the tragic plane crash that claimed the lives of the Lokomotiv Yaroslavl ice hockey team. Prime Minister Vladimir Putin joined mourners at the Arena Yaroslavl (also known as Arena 2000), laying flowers before the coffins of players and staff. Of the 45 people aboard the chartered Yak-42 jet, 43 died when the plane crashed into the banks of the Volga River shortly after takeoff on Wednesday. Thirty-six of the deceased were team members—including coaches and personnel—many of whom were prominent European and former NHL players. Portraits of the victims were displayed on chairs beside their coffins as crowds filed past, leaving flowers and paying silent tribute. The team was en route to Minsk, Belarus, for the opening game of the Kontinental Hockey League (KHL) season. The disaster sent shockwaves through the global ice hockey community and deeply affected the city of Yaroslavl, where the team was a source of immense local pride. Russian investigators confirmed all three engines were functioning normally before impact. Initial suspicions of contaminated fuel at Tunoshna Airport were dismissed after data recorder analysis showed no evidence of fuel failure. Two individuals survived: player Alexander Galimov and crew member Alexander Sizov. Both remain in critical condition in Moscow hospitals, with Galimov suffering burns over 90% of his body. The cause of the crash remains under investigation.

Peaminister Vladimir Putin liitus kurbusega Arena Jaroszlavi (tuntud ka kui Arena 2000), asetades õrnalt lilli kohvikute ees, kus olid meeskonna liikmete ja töötajate surnukehad. 45 inimesest oli lennukil 43, kes hukkusid, kui charterlennuk Yak-42 kukkus peale starti Volga jõe kaldale kesknädalal. article_content: After a quarter-century at the helm, Jeremy Paxman has stepped down from BBC Two’s Newsnight — and the network has named Evan Davis as his successor. Known for his sharp intellect and calm authority on programs like Today and Dragons’ Den, Davis will return to the show where he first rose to prominence in the 1990s as economics editor. His appointment, effective this autumn, comes as a surprise to many who anticipated one of the program’s long-standing female anchors — Laura Kuenssberg, Kirsty Wark, or Emily Maitlis — would take the role. Davis will anchor the program three nights a week. BBC Director General Tony Hall described Davis as an 'outstanding journalist' with a rare ability to engage deeply with complex topics. Newsnight’s editor, Ian Katz, echoed the sentiment, calling Davis’s blend of curiosity, wit, and intellectual rigor exactly what the show needs as it looks to evolve. Davis himself admitted he didn’t believe the news when he first read it in the papers — and joked that he’d failed his personal goal of outlasting John Humphrys on Today. Still, he called the move an exciting challenge and thanked his colleagues at Radio 4, whom he called indispensable. The decision has reignited conversations about gender diversity at the BBC. While the corporation has pledged progress — including a target for 50% of local radio breakfast slots to be held by women by 2014 — the selection of Davis over three accomplished female presenters raised eyebrows. The BBC Trust noted the continued gap between male and female representation on air and urged leadership to implement coordinated strategies for change. Davis isn’t without controversy. In 2012, his interview with then-Chancellor George Osborne drew widespread criticism for what many saw as an overly aggressive, interruptive style. Downing Street called the exchange 'unacceptably hostile.' He also faced backlash for pushing his own views during interviews on Brexit and welfare. Yet supporters argue his tenacity makes him uniquely suited to hold power to account — a core mission of Newsnight. Beyond journalism, Davis holds degrees from Oxford and Harvard, and has authored books on Britain’s economy. He’ll continue hosting The Bottom Line on Radio 4 and Dragons’ Den. Bookmakers, who had odds of 25-1 against Davis landing the job, reported taking just one £3 bet on him — a sign of just how unexpected the announcement was. As he returns to Newsnight, Davis acknowledges the weight of the role — and the hope that viewers will see his return as a fresh chapter, not a step backward.

Tuntud oma terava intellekti ja rahuliku autoriteedi poolest programmides nagu Today ja Dragons’ Den, tagastab Davis programmi, kus ta tõusis esmakordselt tuntusele 1990. aastatel majandustoimetajana. Tema nimetamine, mis jõustub sügisel, on paljude jaoks üllatus, kes ootasid, et üks programmi pikaajalise naissõprade — Laura Kuenssberg, Kirsty Wark või Emily Maitlis — võtab selle rolli. Kuigi korporatsioon on lubanud edusamme — sealhulgas eesmärgi, et 50 protsenti kohalike raadioõhtute algustest peaksid olema naistel 2014. aasta lõpuks — tõi Davisi valimine kolme osutatud naissõprade kõrval välja silma. Lisaks ajakirjandusele on Davisil diplomid Oxfordin ja Harvardi ülikoolidest ja ta on kirjutanud raamatuid Suurbritannia majanduse kohta. Ta jätkab The Bottom Line ja Dragons’ Den esitamist. Bokkide tehased, kes olid 25-1 võimaluste vastu Davisi valimist, teatasid, et võtsid ainult ühe 3 naela panuse temale — märk sellest, kui ootamatult oli teade. article_content: These days, many women are adding another item to their list of body concerns: excess fat around the upper back, underarms, and arms — the very areas hidden beneath bra straps. In response, The Private Clinic on Harley Street has introduced a minimally invasive procedure called Microcannula Tumescent Liposuction, or Microlipo. Designed to target these stubborn pockets of fat, the treatment uses tiny 3mm cannulas and a mild local anesthetic to gently remove fat over a 2- to 3-hour session, starting at £2,600. Since 2010, demand for this service has doubled, with more patients now opting to treat multiple zones at once rather than focusing on just one area. Dr. Puneet Gupta, the clinic’s cosmetic physician and the only practitioner in Europe certified in this technique, emphasizes a holistic approach: he considers how the body looks fully clothed, not just isolated spots. The benefit? No general anesthesia, minimal downtime, and patients can return to daily life almost right away. Meanwhile, other trends reflect similar desires: Sainsbury’s sells a £10 bra marketed to smooth the upper back, while non-invasive fat-freezing treatments like Lipoglaze are seeing surging interest — especially for inner thighs, fueled by the so-called 'thigh gap' trend. Even areas like the knees are now getting attention, thanks to devices like Ultra Lipolyse, which claim to reduce fat and tighten skin simultaneously. Plastic surgeon Nigel Mercer notes a growing number of men seeking liposuction for gynecomastia ('moobs'), reinforcing that body image pressures aren't limited to women — though they remain the primary market for these cosmetic innovations.

article_content: REI Co-op’s 650 Down Jacket remains one of the most practical and affordable insulated layers on the market. The latest update refines the popular 650 Down Jacket 2.0 — now simply called the 650 Down Jacket — with thoughtful upgrades that boost comfort and durability. A key improvement is the shift from a square grid stitching pattern to horizontal baffles, helping distribute warmth more evenly across the torso. While this stitch-through design isn’t as warm as fully baffled construction (common in premium jackets), it keeps the price accessible. The jacket now uses Bluesign-certified ripstop nylon, a tougher, tear-resistant fabric that resists damage without adding bulk — a smart move, since many lightweight down jackets are surprisingly fragile. A subtle but useful addition is the adjustable drawstring at the hem, which seals in warmth by tightening around the waist. The down inside has a 650 fill power, delivering solid warmth relative to its weight — typical for jackets in this price range. Compared to synthetic alternatives, down is lighter, packs smaller, and feels cozier, but it loses insulation when damp and dries slowly. For those avoiding animal products, this is worth noting. The only real drawback? It’s $30 more than the prior version, now priced at $129. Still, with rising down costs industry-wide, this remains one of the best bargains available. article_content: James 'Whitey' Bulger, once feared as Boston’s most brutal crime lord, stood trial for a string of atrocities that terrorized South Boston for over 20 years. Prosecutors painted him as the architect of a violent empire, responsible for 19 murders and widespread extortion — not necessarily as the shooter in every case, but as the mastermind pulling the strings. His alleged partnership with FBI informants, they argued, gave him a shield to operate with impunity. The defense countered by attacking the integrity of the government’s star witnesses — men with long rap sheets who traded testimony for reduced sentences. Attorneys suggested these deals were less about justice and more about convenience, and questioned why the FBI failed for years to stop Bulger despite knowing his crimes. Central to the trial was the question: Was Bulger truly an FBI informant? Prosecutors pointed to documents and testimony showing he fed intelligence on rivals while committing his own atrocities. The defense insisted the agency’s incompetence, not cooperation, allowed Bulger to thrive — and that the government was now using his informant label to distract from its own failures. Emotional moments marked the proceedings. Prosecutor Fred Wyshak described chilling details: Bulger ordering a man shot after demanding repayment, or casually saying 'Drink up, Paulie' near the river where victim Paul McGonagle’s remains were found. Witnesses recalled Bulger napping after killings — a detail meant to underscore his detachment. Though Bulger never took the stand, his outbursts in court — accusing the judge of silencing him and calling the trial a 'sham' — fueled perceptions of a man unwilling to face accountability. Meanwhile, the defense tried to shift blame for two female murders onto Bulger’s associate, Steve Flemmi, suggesting Flemmi’s personal motives outweighed Bulger’s involvement. After 35 days and over 70 witnesses, the jury was left to weigh whether Bulger’s leadership role made him legally responsible for the entire reign of terror — regardless of who pulled the trigger.

Prokurörid kujutasid teda vägivaldse impeeriumi loojana, kes oli vastutav 19 tapmuse ja laialt levinud extorsiooni eest — mitte alati kui tapsja, vaid kui juht, kes veeretas lõike. Advokaadid väitsid, et need kokkulepped olid pigem praktika kui õigluse pärast ja küsisid, miks FBI ei pidanud Bulgerit peatama, kuigi ta kuritegud olid teada. Kohtuprotsessi keskmes oli küsimus: Kas Bulger oli tõesti FBI informaator? Prokurörid viitasid dokumentidele ja testimisele, mis näitasid, et ta andis teavet vaenlaste kohta, samal ajal kui tegi enda kuritegusid. Kaitse väitis, et asutuse puudulikkus, mitte koostöö, võimaldas Bulgeril ellu jääda — ja et valitsus kasutas tema informaatori staatuset, et hoida ära oma enda vigade tähelepanu. Tunneolud olid protsessi osa. Prokurör Fred Wyshak kirjeldas karmi üksikasju: Bulgeri käskis tapma meest, kes oli võlgu 400 000 dollarit, või kuidas ta kergelt ütles 'Joogu, Paulie' kohal, kus leiti ohvri Paul McGonagle jäänused. Bulger ei võtnud sõna, kuigi ta oli kohal olnud kohtus, kus ta süüdistas kohtunikku, et ta on teda vaeselt hoidnud, ja nimetas protsessi 'shami'. article_content: Colorado's Department of Transportation launched a series of satirical public service announcements warning against driving under the influence of marijuana. The campaign, centered on the slogan 'Drive High, Get a DUI,' contrasts legal recreational marijuana use in everyday activities with the clear illegality of operating a vehicle while impaired. In one ad, a man attempts to grill meat while visibly high, repeatedly pressing buttons on a barbecue — unaware that no gas tank is connected. The screen flashes: 'Grilling high is now legal. Driving to get the propane you forgot isn't.' Another features a man joyfully installing a TV while high, performing karate moves and ignoring warnings. When the TV falls and shatters, the message appears: 'Installing your TV while high is now legal. Driving to get a new one isn't.' A third ad shows a man endlessly dribbling a basketball during a game, frustrating teammates. The caption reads: 'Playing ball high is now legal. Driving to see the pros play afterward isn't.' These ads highlight a critical gap in enforcement: unlike alcohol, marijuana cannot be detected via breathalyzer. Colorado law sets a legal limit of 5 nanograms of THC per milliliter of blood — detectable only through blood testing. To combat this challenge, Colorado state troopers undergo nine days of specialized training to become certified Drug Recognition Experts (DREs). According to CBS News, marijuana was cited as a factor in 15% of impaired driving citations in the previous year.

article_content: (CNN) — Dani Pedrosa replicated his 2012 success at the sweltering Sepang circuit on Sunday, but his Honda teammate Marc Marquez took another major step toward clinching the MotoGP world title by finishing a strong second. The 20-year-old Marquez won a thrilling battle with defending champion Jorge Lorenzo of Yamaha, extending his championship lead over the Spaniard to 43 points. Marquez could seal the title next week at Philip Island in Australia — potentially becoming the first rookie to win the MotoGP premier class crown in 35 years. He said overtaking Lorenzo midway through the 20-lap race was deeply satisfying. 'It was a great battle with Jorge. I really enjoyed it,' Marquez told the official MotoGP website. 'Our goal this weekend was to finish ahead of Jorge.' The result left Pedrosa unchallenged to the finish line, securing his third win of the season and cutting Lorenzo’s lead in the standings to just 11 points. Pedrosa took command in 40-degree Celsius heat, passing polesitter Marquez early in the race. 'It’s a great feeling to be back... I’ve come back strong,' said Pedrosa, who crashed in the previous round in Spain after a collision with Marquez. That incident earned Marquez a penalty point — his third of the season — and a formal warning. Lorenzo’s teammate, seven-time world champion Valentino Rossi of Italy, finished fourth, followed by Spanish Honda rider Álvaro Bautista. Britain’s rising star Cal Crutchlow, who started third on the grid, ended up sixth, just ahead of compatriot Bradley Smith. Malaysia hosted the 15th race of the 18-race season. Next up are Australia, Japan, and the season finale in Valencia. Marquez is likely to celebrate his historic title in front of his home fans at the final race, having replaced retired legend Casey Stoner in the Repsol Honda lineup this season.

article_content: These incredible images show a lightning storm above Houston, Texas, captured from an extraordinary vantage point: the edge of space. The stills come from a Vine video posted by NASA astronaut Reid Wiseman, 38, aboard the International Space Station in low Earth orbit. The video, shared on Friday, reveals the raw power of the storm as rapid flashes illuminate the thick cloud layer below. Wiseman, originally from Baltimore, Maryland, has become a leading voice in NASA’s social media outreach, carrying forward the legacy of former ISS commander Chris Hadfield, who famously performed David Bowie’s 'Space Oddity' in microgravity and collaborated with Canadian band Barenaked Ladies via live video link. Earlier this month, Wiseman, along with fellow astronauts Steve Swanson and Alexander Gerst, demonstrated microgravity football skills with acrobatic bicycle kicks and somersaults. Wiseman launched to the ISS on May 28, 2014, aboard a Soyuz rocket from the Baikonur Cosmodrome in Kazakhstan as part of Expedition 40/41. He is scheduled to return to Earth in November 2014 after spending several months in orbit. Before launch, Wiseman shared an emotional farewell with his wife, Carroll, and their two young daughters. A veteran naval aviator and test pilot, Wiseman graduated from Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute in 1997. He earned his wings in 1999, served two Middle East deployments, attended the U.S. Naval Test Pilot School, and later completed a master’s degree at Patuxent River, Maryland. He flew combat missions before being selected for NASA’s astronaut program.

article_content: Peter Wright returned to the Alexandra Palace stage on Friday, sporting his signature loud outfit and extravagant hairstyle. The 2014 World Darts Championship finalist delivered a dominant performance, defeating Gerwyn Price 3-0 in the first round. But it was his attire that stole the spotlight: a bright red shirt paired with festive Christmas trousers, and a meticulously shaved Christmas tree embedded in his beard. Wright’s signature blue-and-white spiky mohican featured additional holiday flair — on one side, a shiny, glued-on snake; on the other, a sprig of mistletoe, a kiss symbol, and another Christmas tree. The entire design took two and a half hours to complete. Wright credited his wife, Jo, for every detail of his look. He joked that she usually needs just two minutes to decide his outfit — but Friday’s creation was an exception. 'The snake is glued on,' he said. 'It’s going to hurt to remove it. I’ll need a long, hot shower to soften the adhesive.' Despite his match-winning focus, Wright remained playful about the spectacle. 'We try and change things,' he explained. 'You can’t be the same all the time. Even people who don’t like me say, “Let’s see what that idiot looks like today” — at least they tune in.' He added with a grin: 'I didn’t even know what she was planning today, and I have no idea what’s coming next round. She tells me, “Sit down, don’t move — I’ll tell you when to stand up.” I used to have a say. Now? I just shut up and do as I’m told. She wears the trousers. She’s the boss.'

article_content: Elson Kambalu never wanted to be boxed in as just another African artist painting lakes and lions for tourists. Even early on, he turned away from the expected — choosing instead to forge his own abstract path. Today, he’s one of Malawi’s most respected contemporary artists, known not just for his bold canvases but for building bridges between creators and collectors. At 40, Kambalu is more than a painter; he’s a catalyst. He founded Art House Africa, a creative hub designed to connect artists with businesses and help them thrive professionally. In a conversation with CNN, he reflected on how a chance meeting with a skeptical gallerist at 28 became his turning point. The gallery owner told him his work wouldn’t sell — too unconventional. But three days later, every piece had sold. That moment changed everything. Though he kept his day job as a loan officer until 31, it was a quiet epiphany — one that struck him in a bathroom stall — that led him to imagine a new kind of art ecosystem. With no formal art schools or managers in Malawi, he saw an opening. When offered a promotion to another city, he said no. He chose to stay and build something new. His art? It’s messy, layered, and defiantly diverse. He paints, sculpts, designs clothes, writes poetry, directs films — and refuses to be labeled. His inspiration? Childhood hunger. Growing up in a large family where meals were scarce, he learned early what it meant to want. Those memories fuel his work: stories of survival, dignity, and quiet resistance among ordinary Africans. He draws from global icons like Picasso, Pollock, and Damien Hirst, as well as Tracey Emin, but his heart beats for the untold histories of his continent. What drives him now isn’t fame — it’s legacy. He started a kids’ art studio because he believes the future of Malawian art lies not just in producing artists, but in nurturing audiences who understand and value their labor. Without education, he says, there can be no true appreciation. And without appreciation, art dies.

Täna on ta üks Malawi kõige austatumaid ajakohaseid kunstnikke, tuntud mitte ainult oma julgete maalide, vaid ka loojate ja kliendite vaheliste silmade ehitamise poolest. 40-aastasena on Kambalu rohkem kui maalija; ta on katalüsaator. Ta asutas Art House Africa, loovaliini, mis on mõeldud ühendama kunstnikke ettevõtetega ja aitama neil professionaalselt areneda. CNN-ga vestluses mõtles ta sellele, kuidas tema 28-aastaselt juhuslik kohtumine skeptilise galleristi ja tema lõikumine sai tema käänukoha. Gallerist ütles talle, et tema tööd ei müü — liiga ebakõlaliselt. Kuid kolm päeva hiljem oli kõik teosed müüdud. See hetk muutis kõike. Malawis puudusid formaalsed kunstikoolid ja kunstijuhtidena. Ta nägi avasõnu. Kui talle pakkuti promootsiooni teise linna, keeldus ta. Ta valis jääda ja ehitada midagi uut. Tema kunst? See on segane, kihtidega ja vastupanuvõimeline. Ta maalib, skulpteerib, disainib riideid, kirjutab luuletusi, režisseerib filme — ja keeldub määratlustest. Tema inspiratsioon? Lapsepõlve näljast. Suure peres, kus toidu osad olid haruldased, õppis ta varakult, mis tähendab soovi. Need mälestused toidavad tema tööd: lugu survest, auastmest ja vaiksest vastupanust tavaliste aafriklaste seas. Ta võtab inspiratsiooni globaalsete ikoonidest nagu Picasso, Pollock ja Damien Hirst, samuti Tracey Emin, kuid tema süda lööb oma kontinendi tuhandete lugude poole. Mis teda täna juhib, ei ole kuulsus — vaid pärand. Ta asutas laste kunstistuudio, sest ta usub, et Malawi kunsti tulevik seisneb mitte ainult kunstnikute valmistamises, vaid ka publiku kasvatamises, kes mõistab ja hindab nende tööd. Ilma hariduseta, ütleb ta, ei saa olla tõelist hindamist. Ja ilma hindamiseta sureb kunst.

article_content: A mother of three drowned after being swept out to sea by a powerful riptide at Famara Beach in Lanzarote, Canary Islands, while her husband tried to save her. Nikki Bate had warned her two sons not to enter the water due to dangerous conditions, moments before entering the sea herself. She soon screamed for help. Her husband, Anthony Bate, 56, dove in to rescue her and managed to grab hold, but the intense current pulled them apart. He watched helplessly as she panicked and drowned. The family had been staying at their holiday home on the island. The tragedy occurred on Thursday afternoon. After returning to the UK, Anthony, from Barrow, Lancashire, said: 'We spent a few hours paddling in the surf, then she said, 'In five minutes, we’re going home.' She went for a swim. But unfortunately, it's one of the most dangerous beaches in the Canaries. My daughter India said she was shouting for help, so I swam out and reached her. The sea was terrible — shocking. I’ve never seen anything like it. We were being battered about and got separated. She panicked and drowned. It was a little mistake with calamitous consequences — this is the tragedy we’re left with.' He added: 'We are all devastated, but we are being strong.' Lifeguards arrived within minutes, pulled both to shore, and worked for at least half an hour to revive Nikki. Anthony praised their tireless efforts and the compassion shown by police and ambulance personnel. Nikki, aged 48, was described by her husband as a wonderful and dedicated mother. She had been married to Anthony for 16 years. Anthony met Nikki 20 years ago at an Asda store in Accrington, bonding over their shared vegetarianism. Originally from Whalley, she was a homemaker and volunteer with Home-Start, supporting families with young children in East Lancashire. She previously owned The Crown Wheel restaurant in Whalley, now known as Amico Mio. The family received consular assistance from the UK Foreign Office and returned to the UK around midnight on Sunday. Famara Beach has a history of deadly currents. In April 2013, British man Steve Potter, 43, died in similar circumstances after being dragged underwater and unable to be revived. Local resident Julie Cliffe-Jones warned: 'Playa de Famara is stunning but dangerous. We urge visitors to stay in shallow water — this is not a swimming beach. It’s famous for its rip tides.' Although red warning flags are flown continuously, there is only one lifeguard station serving the entire two-mile stretch of beach.

article_content: In a heartbreaking case from Daytona Beach, Florida, Luis Toledo, 31, has been charged with second-degree murder after admitting to fatally striking his wife, Yessenia Suarez, 28, during a heated argument. According to police, Toledo, who has martial arts training, claimed he struck her throat in response to her saying she wanted a divorce and had been communicating with another man. He insists he did not harm their two young children—nine-year-old Thalia and eight-year-old Michael—but authorities have since confirmed all three are deceased. Despite this, Toledo refuses to reveal where their bodies are. The family’s home showed signs of blood, and Toledo was seen helping move Suarez’s car to Lake Mary shortly after her disappearance. Known to police as a repeat offender with a history of violent crimes—including burglary, kidnapping, and gun offenses—Toledo has used several aliases over the years, including Michael Garcia, and once served four years in prison under that name. He was initially arrested on a domestic battery charge but later charged with murder after confessing. On the day Suarez was reported missing, Toledo told officers he had slept in his car after an argument and returned to find everyone gone. His attempts to shift blame onto others and his suicide attempt in jail have deepened suspicions. Meanwhile, Suarez’s mother, Felicia Perez, has publicly begged Toledo to tell the truth: 'You know where they are. Please, that’s all I ask.' The investigation continues, with officials still searching for the children’s remains.

Politsei kohaselt väitis Toledo, kes on võitluskunstide treenitud, et ta löögi teda kurvalt kaela, kuna ta ütles, et tahab lahku minna ja oli suhtlemas teise mehega. article_content: Only three U.S. governors have ever been removed from office through a recall election — and now, Wisconsin’s Scott Walker might become the fourth. Voters in Wisconsin head to the polls amid intense backlash over Walker’s 2011 legislation that curtailed collective bargaining rights for public-sector unions. If he loses, Milwaukee’s Democratic mayor, Tom Barrett, would take over, marking just the third time in American history that voters have successfully recalled a sitting governor. The last two were North Dakota’s Lynn Frazier in 1921 and California’s Gray Davis in 2003, according to Rutgers University’s Eagleton Institute of Politics. California stands out as the epicenter of recall politics: every governor elected since 1968 — including icons like Ronald Reagan — has faced at least one recall effort. Altogether, 19 states, plus the District of Columbia, allow citizens to initiate recall elections for governors and other officials. Virginia is unique in requiring a court ruling to remove an official. On the same day, Wisconsin voters will also decide whether to recall Walker’s lieutenant governor and four Republican state senators. The race has drawn millions in campaign funds from across the country, turning the vote into a national political battleground. Analysts say the outcome hinges on grassroots mobilization, not just money. And while President Obama hasn’t publicly weighed in, some wonder if his silence signals a strategic calculation — or simply a recognition that this fight belongs to Wisconsin voters.

article_content: Researchers at the Wake Forest Institute for Regenerative Medicine are developing a revolutionary skin bio-printer inspired by standard inkjet printers. Instead of ink, the device deposits living skin cells harvested from patients to repair severe burns — a potential game-changer for wounded soldiers and civilians alike. Dr. Anthony Atala, the institute’s director, explained that the team began with a commercially available printer, replacing ink cartridges with biocompatible containers holding patient-derived cells. A key innovation is a 3D 'elevator' system that precisely layers new skin tissue over damaged areas without physical contact. The process starts with a tiny skin biopsy — roughly half the size of a postage stamp — extracted using a gentle chemical solution. These cells are then cultivated in a lab until millions are produced. Once ready, they’re loaded into the printer and sprayed in thin, controlled layers directly onto the wound. Unlike conventional inkjet nozzles, the bio-printer uses pressurized jets that allow safe operation from a distance, accommodating diverse body shapes and wound sizes. Depending on the burn’s extent, the entire reconstruction can take minutes to a few hours. The technology is still in pre-clinical trials. While early lab tests have successfully grown healthy skin, full human deployment may take another five years due to rigorous regulatory requirements. Other institutions — including Cornell University and the Medical University of South Carolina — are pursuing similar bio-printing technologies, with ambitions to eventually print complex organs. These efforts will be highlighted at the upcoming American Association for the Advancement of Science conference in Washington. Funded by the U.S. Department of Defense’s Armed Forces Institute of Regenerative Medicine, Wake Forest is set to receive $50 million over five years for this and related regenerative medicine projects. Despite its military funding, researchers emphasize the technology isn’t uniquely designed for combat. 'We’re not making anything military-unique,' said Terry Irgens of the U.S. Army Medical Materiel Development Activity. 'We hope it will benefit both soldiers and civilians.' One remaining challenge is sourcing sufficient skin samples from patients with massive burns. Researchers are working on solutions to overcome this limitation before field deployment.

Instituudi juht Dr Anthony Atala selgitas, et meeskond alustas tavalise kaubamärgi printerist, asendades mustuse kartridid biokompatiibsete konteineritega, mis sisaldavad patsiendi rakke. Oluline innovatsioon on 3D 'tõstukisüsteem', mis täpselt kihi kaupa lisab uut naha kahjustatud alale ilma füüsilise kokkupuuteta. Teised institutsioonid — sealhulgas Cornelli Ülikool ja Lõuna-Carolina Meditsiiniülikool — arendavad sarnaseid bio-printimistehnoloogiaid, kavandades lõpuks keerukate organite printimist. 'Me ei loo midagi sõjaväeliselt unikaalset,' ütles USA sõjaväe meditsiinilise materjali arendamise osakonna programmijuht Terry Irgens. 'Meie eesmärk on aidata nii sõdade kui tsiviilisikuid.' article_content: You can simulate being a football manager in games like Championship Manager—or even manage a zoo in Zoo Tycoon—but there’s no video game called Fantasy Executive Chairman. And for good reason: you think you’re in charge, but you’re not. The real power lies elsewhere. On the pitch, the manager calls the shots—selecting the team, crafting tactics, earning chants from fans. But behind the scenes, the owner writes the checks. They hire and fire managers, approve transfers, and ultimately decide what’s possible. The executive chairman? They look important. They give speeches. But they don’t pick the XI. Their authority ends when the person footing the bill says no. Richard Scudamore, once hailed as football’s most powerful man, couldn’t stop Premier League clubs from using loan deals—even though he publicly opposed them. His role was advisory, not absolute. Nicola Cortese learned this the hard way. As Southampton’s executive chairman, he oversaw a remarkable rise—from League One to the Premier League—and even began to believe he was the architect. But the truth? He was an employee. The money wasn’t his. It belonged to Markus Liebherr, the Swiss industrialist who bought the club in 2009 and died just a year later. After Markus’s death, his daughter Katharina inherited control. She honored his legacy—for a while. Cortese thrived under that umbrella, earning £1.6 million in a single year as the club spent £75 million on players. He spoke as if he were the visionary. But every transfer, every upgrade, every promotion was paid for by Liebherr money. Cortese’s biggest mistake? Forgetting that managers aren’t just department heads—they’re the entire reason the department exists. Lose them, and the whole house collapses. He didn’t realize he was the same: replaceable, dependent, and ultimately expendable. Now, rumors swirl that Katharina wants to sell. She may not care about football. She may not feel the emotional weight her father carried. And honestly? That’s her right. Billionaires don’t owe anyone loyalty. They invest. They walk away. Southampton’s success wasn’t Cortese’s miracle—it was a talented academy, a loyal fanbase, and a new stadium, all rescued by cash. Players like Gareth Bale, Theo Walcott, and Adam Lallana were already developing before Cortese arrived. He didn’t create the foundation—he just spent wisely on it. Pochettino stayed after a five-minute chat with Katharina. Not because Cortese left—but because he still sees a future. But if a richer club comes knocking, he’ll go. No coach quits over an executive’s exit. They quit when the money dries up. Cortese did a solid job. But he was a banker, not a builder. And bankers? They get paid to manage other people’s fortunes. Sometimes, the fortune runs out—or the owner decides to cash out.

Tegelik võim asub mujal. Laua taga otsustab treener — valib koondise, loob taktikat ja teenib fännide laulu. Kuid tagaotsas kirjutab omanik kontrollid. Ta palkab ja eraldab treenereid, kinnitab läbirääkimised ja otsustab lõplikult, mis on võimalik. Juht? Ta näeb välja oluline. Ta räägib. Kuid ta ei vali XI-d. Tema volitused lõpevad siis, kui raha andja ütleb ei. Richard Scudamore, kellele ükskord anti tiitel kõige võimsama inimesena jalgpallis, ei suutnud takistada Premier League klubide laenukasutust — kuigi ta avalikult neid vastu oli. Tema roll oli nõustav, mitte absoluutne. Nicola Cortese õppis seda raske viisil. Ta oli Southamptoni juht, kes juhitas märkimisväärset tõusu — League One-st Premier League’i — ja hakkas uskuma, et ta on selle ehitaja. Kuid tegelikkus? Ta oli töötaja. Raha ei kuulunud talle. See kuulus Šveitsi töösturile Markus Liebherrile, kes ostis klubi 2009. aastal ja suri üks aasta pärast. Markuse surma järel päris tema tütar Katharina kontrolli. Ta kinkis oma isa visiooni — vähemalt mõne aja jooksul. Cortese kasvas selle varjus, teenides ühes aastas 1,6 miljonit naela, samal ajal kui klubi kulutas 75 miljonit naela mängijatele. Ta rääkis nagu oleks ta visiooniline juht. Kuid igasüsteem, igas edusamm ja igas promootioon oli makstud Liebherri raha eest. Cortese suurim viga? Milljonärid ei võta keegi vastutust. Nad investeerivad. Nad lahkuvad. article_content: A music teacher at Hazel Harvey Peace Elementary School in Fort Worth, Texas, is under investigation after students alleged he racially segregated his fifth-grade class and made offensive remarks about Black students’ upbringing. According to parents, the incident occurred on Friday, when the teacher reportedly separated students by race, called the class 'stupid,' and told Black students, 'I know where y’all from' and 'I can tell neither one of y’all get punished at home.' Sandra Lee, mother of one student, said her daughter recounted the event immediately after school. Lee visited the school on Monday to formally report the incident, stating, 'Everything that was going on was racist.' The Fort Worth Independent School District confirmed it became aware of the allegations on Friday and is gathering statements from students. The teacher involved has not been officially named, though Edgar Cajas is listed as the school’s only music teacher on its website — his connection to the incident has not been confirmed. Some parents also mentioned prior concerns about inappropriate content in music class earlier this year, including a film containing profanity and violence. District spokesman Clint Bond stated: 'Campus and District leadership have been aware of the allegations since last Friday. Once the facts are known, appropriate action will be taken.'
